_comment: Guided tour for Region MLE. Steps point at real controls and wait for the user to press them — there is deliberately no 'do it for me' button, because someone who watched a button being pressed has not learned where it is. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: One lifetime per region, and none of them found here
steps.text:
This tool fits a single fluorescence lifetime per region by Poisson maximum likelihood — the 2I* estimator, on the parallel and perpendicular decays together.

It does not segment. The regions come from the Spot Finder, the panel above, or from a saved label image. That separation is deliberate: a fit that finds its own regions cannot be shown what it is about to fit, which is exactly how a tuned preview and the run that followed it stopped agreeing.

Seven steps, about two minutes.

steps.title: Start with lifetimes you already know
steps.text:
A fitted lifetime is a number with nothing to check it against. So start with a simulated field: four objects with lifetimes of 1.0, 3.6, 2.2 and 0.6 ns, its own IRF measurement, and the standard detection already run over it.

Everything below is then filled in the way a real analysis would fill it, and the answers are known.

await.hint: Press 🧪 Load demo. It simulates the field (a few seconds the first time), detects the regions, and fills this panel in.

steps.title: The IRF is a measurement, not a shape
steps.text:
The instrument response is measured on the same optics and detectors as the sample — here a simulated scatterer with the same micro-time axis. It is what lets the fit deconvolve rather than assume.

A fit given an analytic, noiseless IRF against noisy data is being handed an advantage no measurement provides, which is why the demo simulates one instead of drawing a Gaussian.

steps.title: Which detection to fit
steps.text:
A measurement can hold more than one detection — the same field segmented two ways, to be compared. Detection names which one this fit answers for, and the fit answers for exactly those regions and no others.

Min photons is the honesty threshold: a region below it is not fitted, and keeps a row with NaN parameters rather than vanishing. A missing row would silently shift every result after it when tables are merged.

steps.title: What is being fitted, and what is held
steps.text:
τ is the lifetime; γ is the scatter fraction; r0 and ρ describe the anisotropy. For a first look, fix r0 and ρ — with a few thousand photons per region the data cannot support four free parameters, and freeing them buys a worse-determined τ rather than more information.

l1 and l2 are the polarisation mixing corrections of the objective, and belong with the detector setup rather than with the sample.

steps.title: Look at the regions before fitting them
steps.text: Preview measures the regions about to be fitted without fitting them — area, brightness, the background rate around them. It resolves the regions through the same call the run uses, so what is previewed is what is fitted; there is no second segmentation to disagree with it.

await.hint: Press 👁️ Preview, then press ▶ Run to fit.

steps.title: Read the decay, not only the number
steps.text:
Open the Decay tab and select a region. You get the data, the fitted model, the IRF and the background on a log axis, with the weighted residuals above sharing the time axis — so a systematic deviation lines up with the channel that caused it. It is the same panel the burst-wise MLE draws, because a region and a burst are the same measurement under different membership rules.

Check the fitted τ against the demo's 1.0, 3.6, 2.2 and 0.6 ns. The long ones come back a few percent low, and that is real: a 3.6 ns decay is not finished inside this simulation's 8.2 ns excitation period.
